angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 542,646 km at 110.18 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.0760 +/- 0.0167 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 110.18 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.78 +/- 0.07 solar radii from Grziwa et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-31 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016AJ....152..132G/abstract): 542,646 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.91 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Grziwa et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-31 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016AJ....152..132G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5280 +/- 70 K from Grziwa et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-31 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016AJ....152..132G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Grziwa et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-31 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016AJ....152..132G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-31.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.613, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
